subject: Lyra Analytics SSQ: data classification, access diagram and DPA handoff
messages:
From: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@lyraanalytics.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lyraanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lyra SSQ kickoff + initial attachments

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're starting the security questionnaire (attached) for our LLM pilot and need clarifications on a few items before we can sign the DPA and complete procurement. High-level asks:

- A short dataflow diagram showing where PII is processed and where vector embeddings (if any) are stored.
- Confirmation of data classification labels Redwood will honor for Lyra (PII, sensitive PII, non-PII) and how they map to retention buckets.
- Who holds the encryption keys (Redwood KMS vs customer BYOK) and whether we can get a key custody attestation.
- A list of subprocessors that will touch customer plaintext or derived telemetry, and whether any of those subprocessors are located outside the US.
- Any DPA redlines you expect (we're sharing our standard DPA in parallel).

Attached: Lyra_SSQ_v0.xlsx (SSQ + sample dataset mappings). Can you confirm a reasonable timeline for answers and whether a technical handoff call Monday would make sense?

Regards,
Emma Ruiz
Security & Privacy Program Manager
Lyra Analytics

Attachment: Lyra_SSQ_v0.xlsx (XLSX spreadsheet, 220 KB)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@lyraanalytics.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@lyraanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lyra SSQ kickoff + initial attachments

Emma — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick summary and proposed next steps:

1) Timeline: we'll return a consolidated SSQ response and a dataflow diagram by EOD Monday (26 Oct).
2) Meeting: propose a 60-min technical handoff Tue 10/27 at 10:00 PT to walk the diagram and DPA redlines.
3) Attachments: initial draft answers and a native dataflow PNG attached for review.

High-level answers inline:
- Data classification: we will adopt Lyra's labels. In practice we map PII => tokenization/pseudonymization pipelines + 90-day short retention; sensitive PII => isolated buckets and 30-day retention unless customer requests longer; non-PII => standard logs retention. We'll include explicit mappings in the SSQ document.
- Embeddings: by default embeddings are treated as derived data. If Lyra opts to treat embeddings as PII/identifiers, we will isolate and apply the same access controls (lets discuss).
- Key custody: Redwood offers both platform-managed KMS and BYOK via customer KMS (supported for Dedicated and Private deployments). We'll note the attestation options.
- Subprocessors: see draft list in attached PDF. Most subprocessors are cloud infra providers in the US, with CDN/edge caching partners in other regions for performance — none of those partners will have access to plaintext unless explicitly configured.

Attachments: Lyra_SSQ_Answers_v1.pdf, dataflow-diagram.png

I'll leave Kim and Connor to add technical detail and DPA redline notes.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Lyra_SSQ_Answers_v1.pdf (PDF, 85 KB); dataflow-diagram.png (PNG, 48 KB)
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lyraanalytics.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@lyraanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Lyra SSQ kickoff + initial attachments

Thanks Mateo — helpful. Two follow-ups from engineering/security:

- Encryption specifics: can you confirm algorithms and whether per-customer key rotation is supported? If BYOK, can we do HSM-backed keys (we use AWS KMS with CloudHSM for other vendors).
- Cross-border subprocessors: you mentioned CDNs in other regions. Do you have a current list and country locations for subprocessors that may cache derived data (embeddings or telemetry)? For regulatory reasons we need to know whether caches could end up in the EU or APAC.

Also, David on our procurement team will want to know if Redwood can accept a limited onshore processing clause for EU-sourced PII (i.e., guarantee processing only in our US region).

Best,
Daniel

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Lyra SSQ technical + DPA redline suggestions

Team — notes to consolidate before the external call:

1) Encryption and key custody
- Algorithms: AES-256-GCM at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit. We support per-customer key rings and rotation every 90 days by default; rotation schedule can be customized for Dedicated/Private customers. For BYOK: we support AWS KMS and customer HSMs via KMIP — can provide attestation (SOC2 control reference) and key usage logs.

2) Subprocessors and caching
- Current subprocessor list (short): primary cloud provider (us-east-1), long-term storage (us-west-2), CDN partner (global edge nodes), telemetry processor (US & EU). We'll mark which subprocessors may run in EU/APAC for derived caches and provide country-level details in the finalized SSQ.
- Policy: caches do not contain plaintext PII. We apply prefix/KV caching for model state — only embeddings/derived vectors may be cached; customer may opt-out of remote caching for sensitive datasets.

3) Data classification and retention mapping (proposal for DPA annex)
- Add annex table: Lyra label => Redwood handling => retention bucket => access role. Example row: "sensitive_pii" => isolated storage + restricted IAM role + 30-day retention + audit logs forwarded to Lyra.

4) Onshore processing carveout
- We can offer an onshore processing guarantee for EU-sourced PII only under Dedicated or Private (customer-provisioned region) with contractual SLA and additional fees. For Hosted customers we can offer regional routing preferences and contractual commitments up to the extent of our current infra footprint.

5) DPA redlines (quick list)
- Add: subprocessor notification window 30 days + right to object; enumeration of subprocessors as an exhibit; specific audit evidence for key custody.
- Clarify: 'processing' definition to explicitly include derived data (embeddings) and telemetry.

6) Next steps
- Connor: assemble country-level subprocessors list and KMS attestation snippet.
- Marissa: produce the annex table and update the SSQ PDF.
- Mateo: propose times for the external call (we already suggested Tue 10/27 10:00 PT).

Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ruiz <emma.ruiz@lyraanalytics.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@lyraanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Finalized SSQ answers, dataflow diagram, and DPA redline (next steps)

Hi Emma / Daniel — thanks for the follow-ups and patience. Attached are the consolidated artifacts after our internal review:

- Lyra_SSQ_Answers_v1.pdf: finalized answers, including country-level subprocessor mapping and explicit handling for derived data.
- dataflow-diagram.png: annotated with storage/enclave boundaries and where KV/prefix caches are used.
- DPA_Redline_Lyra.docx: proposed contractual language for subprocessor notification, onshore processing carveout options, and an annex table mapping Lyra labels to retention buckets.

Quick summary of the commitments in the attachments:
- Encryption: AES-256-GCM at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit, per-customer key rings available; BYOK supported (AWS KMS + HSM). Key rotation configurable; attestation extract included.
- Subprocessors: attached list includes country/region for each subprocessor and identifies which partners may have edge nodes in EU/APAC. No subprocessors have access to plaintext unless explicitly enabled via customer integration.
- Onshore processing: we can contractually guarantee processing within the US only for Dedicated or Private deployments; for Hosted we provide routing preferences and transparency in the DPA.
- Embeddings: by default classed as derived data; can be scoped to PII handling on request.

Next steps: please review the attached redline and SSQ. If acceptable, let's lock a 60-minute call Tue 11/2 at 10:00 PT to walk the DPA redlines and sign-off path (Connors will bring the subprocessors manifest and Kim will walk the annex table). I've attached the draft redline and shared the folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_shared_drive

If you need edits faster, we're happy to do an async review and incorporate comments in the docx.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
m: +1 415-555-0168
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
